prose: Total GDP measures economic size, not prosperity. The ranking correlates with population: four of the ten largest economies by output are also among the ten most populous countries (the United States, China, India, and Russia). The GDP per capita ranking divides output by population and produces a different top ten entirely, led by Luxembourg at 74th in total GDP.

{{overlapCount}} of {{firstYear}}'s top ten economies remain in {{latestYear}}'s top ten: {{overlapList}}. That stability reflects a structural concentration of output: the top three economies alone account for a disproportionate share of global GDP.

faq.q: Which country has the largest economy in {{latestYear}}?
faq.a: {{leaderName}} leads at {{leaderValueFmt}}, followed by {{rank2Name}} at {{rank2ValueFmt}} and {{rank3Name}} at {{rank3ValueFmt}}.

faq.q: How does this differ from GDP per capita?
faq.a: GDP measures total economic output; GDP per capita divides that total by population. A country can rank high on total GDP but low on GDP per capita if it has a large population. The GDP per capita ranking is available as a separate dataset in this library.

faq.q: Which country climbed the GDP rankings most since {{firstYear}}?
faq.a: Among {{latestYear}}'s top ten, {{climberName}} recorded the largest climb, rising from {{climberRankFirstYearOrd}} in {{firstYear}} to {{climberLatestRankOrd}} in {{latestYear}}. The downloadable CSV includes the complete rank history.

faq.q: Are these figures adjusted for inflation?
faq.a: No. Values are in current US dollars as reported by the World Bank. Changes over time reflect both real growth and US-dollar inflation; within-year rankings are unaffected.

faq.q: How often is this data updated?
faq.a: The World Bank publishes updated GDP estimates annually. This page is rebuilt from the latest release, retrieved {{retrievedAtHuman}}.

methodology: Figures are gross domestic product in current US dollars as published in the {{sourceLink}} (indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.CD), retrieved {{retrievedAtHuman}}. Rankings are computed among all economies with reported data for each year; economies with no reported value in a given year are excluded from that year's ranking. Because values are nominal, changes over time reflect both real growth and US-dollar inflation; within-year rankings are unaffected. Trajectory sparklines index each economy's series to its own {{firstYear}}–{{latestYear}} range and are not comparable in level across rows.
